hourly.summary: Arsenal fans are stewing in that familiar, specific frustration after dominating Dortmund for 90 minutes but only walking away with a point — 15 shots, one goal, and Arteta claiming they need 'luck' to finish games. The attacking profligacy has sparked the usual January transfer panic (sign a striker, any striker) and tactical nitpicking, but underneath the grumbling there's a resigned acceptance that this team is still very good, just infuriatingly inefficient. Classic Arsenal: top of the league, in the CL mix, and somehow making everyone's blood pressure spike.

daily.summary: Arsenal fan sentiment rebounded significantly over the course of the day, shifting from frustration (4/10) after a 2-2 draw at Newcastle that dealt a 'major title blow' and sparked injury fears, to anticipation (7/10) ahead of the Champions League clash with Dortmund. The morning's inquest into dropped points and women's team management questions gave way to quiet confidence in the Saliba-Gabriel defensive axis and excitement about the recruitment machine's activity. While women's team concerns persist across both snapshots, the men's side narrative flipped from crisis mode to European-night optimism.

weekly.summary: After riding a wave of euphoric confidence through mid-week — fueled by contract extensions, academy breakthroughs, and table-topping form — Arsenal fan sentiment collapsed dramatically over the weekend. A catastrophic Newcastle draw, Raya's injury scare, and the women's team's managerial crisis triggered a plunge from near-peak optimism (9/10) to structural anxiety (4/10), leaving the fanbase convinced their fragile lead could evaporate at any moment.
